newSolution: \(\log ab\) is defined only when \(ab > 0\), so \(a\) and \(b\) are non-zero and have the same sign. Then \(\log ab - \log|b| = \log\dfrac{ab}{|b|}\). If \(b > 0\) then \(|b| = b\), so \(\dfrac{ab}{|b|} = a\), and here \(a > 0\), giving \(a = |a|\). If \(b < 0\) then \(|b| = -b\), so \(\dfrac{ab}{|b|} = -a\), and here \(a < 0\), giving \(-a = |a|\). Either way the quotient is \(|a|\), so the expression equals \(\log|a|\). The alternative \(\log a\) is not valid in general: when \(a\) and \(b\) are both negative it is undefined, while \(\log|a|\) holds throughout the domain. Hence (B).
whatChanged: Replaced the false parenthetical (b/|b| = plus-or-minus 1, which only yields log of plus-or-minus a) with the domain argument ab>0 forcing a and b to share a sign, worked out for b>0 and b<0 separately, plus a line saying why log a is not universally valid.

newSolution: Change of base gives the chain rule \(\log_x y \cdot \log_z x = \log_z y\). So \(bc = \log_{36}24 \cdot \log_{48}36 = \log_{48}24\), and hence \(abc = a\,(bc) = \log_{24}12 \cdot \log_{48}24 = \log_{48}12\). Therefore \(1 + abc = \log_{48}48 + \log_{48}12 = \log_{48}(48 \cdot 12) = \log_{48}576 = \log_{48}\left(24^{2}\right) = 2\log_{48}24 = 2bc\). Hence (C).
whatChanged: Replaced the bare appeal to a standard identity with the full three-step change-of-base chain (bc = log_48 24, abc = log_48 12, then 1 + abc = log_48 576 = 2 log_48 24), so the answer is derived rather than cited.

newSolution: \(\log_4 18 = \dfrac{\log_2 18}{\log_2 4} = \dfrac{\log_2 18}{2} = \dfrac{1 + \log_2 9}{2}\). Now \(\log_2 9\) is irrational: it is positive, so if it were rational we could write \(\log_2 9 = p/q\) with \(p, q\) positive integers, giving \(2^{p} = 9^{q}\) - impossible, since the left side is even and the right side is odd. Finally, if \(\dfrac{1 + \log_2 9}{2}\) were rational then \(\log_2 9\) would be rational as well, so the whole expression is irrational. Hence (B).
whatChanged: Kept the correct rewrite to (1 + log_2 9)/2 and added the missing proof: the parity contradiction 2^p = 9^q (even = odd) showing log_2 9 is irrational, then the step carrying that irrationality through to (1 + log_2 9)/2.
